content.comment_body: Hello everyone, How can I pause my program or its timers so they keep their current value when paused? Specifically, I want the timers (and program) to stop when the pause button (Input3) is pressed, and when Input3 is released, the timers should resume from where they left off. I have attached an example program for reference. The program is for monitoring; if I2 doesn't produce a pulse within 24 seconds, it triggers an error and the user must press an error acknowledgment button. Thank you! Best Regards, [user_name] Finland PS: Apologies for my English, it's not my strongest language.

Hello, Here is your program with the following changes: 1. I replaced your original timer with a retentive on-delay timer and enabled retentive functionality. 2. Timer B002 is now configured with retention as well. Please check whether this adjustment meets your requirements. Regards

Hi, Unfortunately, this modification doesn't behave as I expected. The program still triggers an error even when the I2 pulse comes within 24 seconds, and I can't restart the timer using the error acknowledgment button. Regards, [user_name]
Hello, I hope this advice is helpful to you. Best regards from Argentina.

Hello, Thank you for your help! I think I should explain my system in more detail to clarify things. In my system, there's monitoring of the greasing process: a sensor sends a pulse when grease enters the system. If no pulse arrives within 24 hours (24 seconds in the simulation), the controller signals an error so the service technician can check. If the pause button is pressed, the greasing function stops (another system controls the pumps), and the sensor doesn't send a pulse. I don't want unnecessary error alerts during maintenance. That's why I don’t reset the timer on pause; if the timer reads 12 hours and gets reset, that greasing point could remain without grease for much longer than intended. So, my goal is to pause timer B001 when needed. Hope my explanation makes sense, as I mentioned earlier that English isn't my native language. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced challenges pausing timers in programmable logic controller projects, needing timers that remember their current value during a pause and resume seamlessly. Early attempts using retentive timers did not meet expectations, as errors occurred even when the proper pulse was received, and timers couldn't reliably be reset through the acknowledgment button. Community members worked together, eventually providing an effective solution, and users expressed strong appreciation for the fast and helpful support provided.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want the ability to pause and resume timers within their controller logic, with timer values retained through pauses to avoid incorrect error states during maintenance. They expect the application to support reliable acknowledgment and error reset features, as well as prevention of unnecessary error notifications during legitimate pauses.
